hook.line: When Tomás's neighbour insists on bringing food to the café, he wants to say "you really don't have to" without sounding rude. Spanish has a warm way to lift the duty.
hook.es: No hace falta que traigas nada.
hook.en: You don't need to bring anything. (to a friend)

examples.es: No hace falta que traigas nada.
examples.en: You don't need to bring anything. (to a friend)

examples.es: No hace falta que vengas temprano.
examples.en: You don't need to come early. (to a friend)

examples.es: No hace falta que pague ahora.
examples.en: You don't need to pay now. (formal)
You all don't need to wait.
You've no reason to apologise. (to a friend)

rule:
To say "you don't need to", use *no hace falta que* plus a verb in its wish form. For *tú*, *-ar* verbs end in *-es* and the others in *-as*: *traes* becomes *traigas*, *vienes* becomes *vengas*. For *usted* the endings are *-e* and *-a*: *pague*, *venga*. For "you all" add *n*: *esperen*.

For reassurance use *no tienes por qué* (or *no tiene por qué*) plus a plain infinitive, with no *que*.

Both only remove an obligation. They do not forbid anything.
smallPrint: Teachers call the wish form the subjunctive. It follows *que* here because the speaker is not stating a fact, only lifting a duty.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *traes* or *traigas* and type the whole sentence: *No hace falta que ___ nada.* (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No hace falta que traigas nada.
accept: No hace falta que traigas nada
yourTurn.why: After *que* the verb takes its wish form, and *traer* becomes *traigas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You don't need to come early. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No hace falta que vengas temprano.
accept: No hace falta que vengas temprano
yourTurn.why: *Venir* changes to *vengas* after *no hace falta que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You don't need to pay now. (to an older customer, formal)
yourTurn.answer: No hace falta que pague ahora.
accept: No hace falta que pague ahora

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You've no reason to apologise. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *No tienes por qué* is followed by a plain infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it to speak to several people: *No hace falta que esperes.*
Type in Spanish: You've no reason to explain it to me. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: The pronouns attach to the end of the infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: No hace falta que traes nada.
pitfalls.right: No hace falta que traigas nada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* here the verb needs its wish form, *traigas*.

pitfalls.right: No hace falta que traigas nada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *No debes* sounds like a ban; *no hace falta* just lifts the duty.

pitfalls.wrong: No tienes por qué que te disculpes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *No tienes por qué* takes a plain infinitive, with no *que*.

personal: Someone offers to bring something to your next gathering. Type what you would tell them with *no hace falta que*.
